claims.statement: Revenue target of Rs 550 crore for FY25, implying over 30% growth from FY24
Capex planned at Rs 60 crore for FY25, primarily for future projects like Project Titan
Gear grinding capacity shortfall rectified; sufficient capacity installed for projected growth including buffer
Noida plant shifted to 32,000 sq ft facility in Sector 80; fully operational without a single day of production loss
Project Titan (parking lock mechanism for German OEM) on track: functional build samples by July end, series production line by Feb 2025, mass production by Aug 2026
EBITDA margin guided at 20-23% range for FY25 as scale grows; FY24 EBITDA margin at 24.09%
H2 FY25 expected to be 20-25% higher than H1 FY25; full-year 37% growth target will not be met
Q1 FY25 EBITDA down ~4% YoY despite 18% revenue growth due to adverse product mix, higher tooling consumption, and fixed cost absorption
Capex budget for FY25 under review; likely reduction from planned levels to lower finance cost
Green energy capacity fully operational: 4 MW captive solar (live from 20 July), 1.3 MW rooftop solar, and IEX trading started first week of August
Advanced discussions with European passenger car OEM for new ICE/hybrid/EV platform; decision expected by year-end
New orders received: Pinion (e-bicycle), FCC India (clutch gears), Adler (clutch gears); commercial supplies started for Adler
Actively pursuing agricultural/industrial segment; US trip planned next month for potential customer convention
Revisiting approved FY25 capex budget; deferring non-critical spend pending customer forecasts post-holidays; revised budget targeted by AGM.
Focus on utilizing existing spare capacity; new capex only linked to growth trajectory and balancing needs.
EBITDA margin aspiration 20-23% maintained; domestic business win (same product as European) will have margins between export and typical domestic (15-16%).
RACL will still grow in FY25 but at a reduced pace vs 30-35% historical; long-term growth bar unchanged.
Revised sales plan to 16% growth from earlier 30-35% target
Management expects clarity on H2 forecasts before Christmas
Received new nomination from BMW for electric sports car drive train parts, commercial production from 2026
Project Titan first sample phase completed successfully in under six months, mass production expected August 2026
EBITDA margin dropped to 21.09% in H1 FY25 from 25.09% in H1 FY24 due to higher depreciation and finance costs
Domestic margins slightly lower than exports but balanced by faster receivables and shorter validation cycles
Invested Rs 22.28 crore in H1 FY25 vs Rs 57 crore in H1 FY24; postponed some investments to next year
Committed Rs 250 crore investment by November 2026 under UP government incentive scheme, already invested ~150 crore
Current capacity can support ~Rs 550 crore revenue at 70-75% utilisation; benchmark is 75-80%
New manufacturing facility UDYAM inaugurated for BMW electric car parking lock mechanism
Mass production at UDYAM plant expected to start August 2026
FY26 revenue projected at 525 crores ±5%
EBITDA margins sustained in 21-24% range despite headwinds
BMW electric car project plant inaugurated, sampling started, SOP end of 2026
Nominated for BMW Motorrad shifting mechanism for R1000 and R1300 models
Nominated for entire drivetrain of TVS Norton motorcycles, commercial production expected early next year
Capex for FY25 on track as planned, no major changes
Capex prioritization underway, will not delay growth due to funding
Target EBITDA margin range 20-25%, currently at 22%
BMW plant 20,000 sq ft, green electricity, one shift, fully commissioned for prototyping
Venus project to share Titan platform, new building by end of year
FY25 addition of fixed assets INR 110.87 crore vs INR 54.31 crore FY24
Project Udyam mass production on track for August 2026
Project Venus prototypes in advanced prototyping phase, first prototypes for assembly and testing in Q2 FY25-26
Project Crystal for steering system supply to leading American passenger car OEM pickup truck platform
RACL receiving confirmed delivery schedules from KTM AG, adopting precautionary approach until KTM fully stabilized
FY26 revenue target of 500-525 crores with +/- 5% range
FY26 capex plan of 45-50 crores to be funded 75% by debt and 25% by equity
Approximately 150 crores capex required for next year to support growth trajectory
Current capacity sufficient for FY26 target of 500-525 crores with 5-10% cushion for seasonal demand
Company policy not to disclose order book as they are non-binding customer forecasts
EBITDA margins sustained at 21-22% quarterly, FY25 at 22% vs 24% in FY24
Target to maintain EBITDA margins in 20-25% range with finance cost reduction supporting improvement
Bhumi Pujan conducted for new manufacturing facility at Gajraula on April 30, 2025 to expand capacity for future projects
Long-term vision to achieve 1000 crores revenue in 3-4 years (by FY29-30) with roadmap in place
Nomination for transmission parts from largest premium 2-wheeler manufacturer SOP January 2026 at Noida plant
Nomination for shift drum for ATV from BRP Canada 150000 parts per annum mass production 2026
Capacity expansion at Noida Unit for new 2-wheeler transmission parts project
New nomination from Indian 2-wheeler OEM for high-volume premium segment project; commercial supplies expected from February 2026
New order from BRP Canada for shifting drum mechanism, ~150,000 parts per annum with +/-20% flexibility; commercial supply expected FY26
Registered as approved vendor with BHEL enabling direct RFQ participation without tendering for precision engineered components
Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 24.83% vs 21.11% in Q1 FY25, up ~3.72%; PBT margin 10.42% vs ~8% last year
Gross profit margin 74.57% in Q1 FY26 vs 71.65% in Q1 FY25
Heavy investment in futuristic technologies (ERC, steer-by-wire, parking lock, steering systems, e-bike gearbox, axle assemblies) over last 2-3 years; scaling up as adoption increases
Building capacity for BRP shifting drum order up to ~180,000 parts per annum
Capex for current financial year is around 50 crores; next two years' capex not yet finalized
Targeting budgeted turnover for FY26 as disclosed in last two board meetings
New high-volume two-wheeler order won two days ago; will use existing idle capacity initially, capex needed later for ramp-up
Capex for projects launching in FY26 will finish this year
Project Venus (BMW cars) prototyping ongoing, SOP next year; ZF steering project prototyping done, validations ongoing, SOP in FY27-28
EBITDA margin benchmark 20-25%; not stationary due to external factors like tariffs
Existing idle capacity used for new two-wheeler order; no immediate capex; capex later for high-volume ramp-up
Growth ~25-30% in FY26 expected from new projects starting in second half (including Jan 26 nomination)
New transmission parts nomination from a premium 2-wheeler OEM with SOP July 2027 at Gajraula plant
Management expects H2 FY26 to be better than H1 and sees double-digit revenue growth of 14-15% for FY26 versus FY25.
Vision to reach INR 1,000 crore revenue in the next three to five years.
Capex for FY26 is about INR 50 crore, likely to be maintained or slightly lower; FY27 capex still being compiled.
Received second nomination for transmission parts from a large premium 2-wheeler OEM; SOP expected July 2027 at Gajraula plant.
TVS RTX 310 and Norton projects launched; production started in November 2025, volumes expected to pick up in 2026.
BMW parking lock mechanism project in pre-series phase; SOP expected 2026.
EBITDA margin maintained above 24% in Q1 and Q2 FY26; Q2 EBITDA margin 24.25%, H1 24.52%.
Participated in defence manufacturing conclave at Jabalpur (Nov 7-9, 2025) to explore entry into defence sector as a sustainable long-term initiative.
FY26-27 revenue target INR 565.00 crore (+5%)
FY26-27 HT plant replacement Gajraula INR 33.88 crore
FY26-27 capacity expansion Gajraula INR 30.04 crore
FY26-27 capacity expansion Noida INR 4.35 crore
FY26-27 HT + rooftop solar Noida INR 9.17 crore
New business nomination from ZF for EPS steering components for North American trucks, SOP FY27-28
New HT plant at Gajraula expected operational by February 2027
Noida plant expansion adding ~27,760 sq. ft. built-up area
Venus Plant Gajraula infrastructure completed, trial runs successful, ready for BMW car SOP end of year
FY27 revenue target of Rs 565 crore plus/minus 5%, implying ~17% growth over FY26
New electric heat treatment plant at Gajraula targeted operational by February 2027; Noida expansion adds 27,760 sq ft for new projects and backward integration
Premium two-wheeler customer doubled volume ask from 10,000 to 20,000 units; production started January 2026
Q3 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 24.93% vs 22.86% YoY; consolidated 24.8% vs 23.8% YoY; PBT margin jump driven by lower finance cost after debt repayment
FY26 revenue growth maintained at 18-20%; 9M at Rs 365 crore implies FY26 ~Rs 485-500 crore
Heat treatment replacement at Gajraula (Rs 33.88 cr) and new setup at Noida (Rs 9.17 cr) total ~Rs 43 cr for backward integration; balance Rs 34.5 cr for core capacity expansion at both plants
Budgeted capex plan for FY 2026-27 is Rs. 77.45 Cr
Addition of Fixed Assets was INR 81.77 Crore in FY 2025-26
FY27 revenue guidance maintained at 565 crores plus/minus 5%
Budgeted capex for FY27 is 77.45 crores with corresponding bank debt to be availed
Royal Enfield project won in January 2026 for 350cc motorcycle engine gears; commercial production expected August-September 2026
Kawasaki Japan awarded high-volume project with 15 parts; one part started, pilot lots submitted, mass production expected January 2027
Project Titan and Venus (BMW electric car reduction gearbox) final sign-off in August 2026; mass production start October-November 2026
Project Crystal (electric power steering for US market with ZF Rane) sampling 600 sets under validation in Mexico and US; focus for prototyping with huge capacity investment planned next year
Commercial track segment (electric power steering for truck with ZF) samples submitted; SOP expected September-October 2026
Shift drum project (non-gear transmission component) SOP next month; 150,000 per annum volume with 6-7 part numbers to add over next year
Consolidated EBITDA margin improved from 22.34% to 25.21% in FY26; standalone EBITDA margin improved from 22.52% to 25.26%
Digital smart factory Industry 4.0 implemented for BMW projects with zero paper documentation and end-to-end traceability from steel mill to finished product
Capex for FY27 disclosed at 77.4 crores, with ~40 crores for heat treatment replacement and 30-35% for additional capacity
Heat treatment plant construction started Jan 2026, building completion expected Oct 2026, equipment arrival Sep-Oct 2026, trial production planned Jan 2027
New heat treatment plant will switch from LPG to electric furnaces, replacing 30+ year old equipment, fully commissioned by end FY27
BMW SOP: Level 1 approval done, conditional shipping started, final sign-off scheduled 24 Oct 2026, pilot supplies moving to customer cards
Royal Enfield commercial supplies started Jan 2026, nominated for ~10,000 sets/month, currently sustaining 7,500-8,000/month on 350cc engine
Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA 32.19 cr (25.11% margin) up 18% YoY, PBT 16.82 cr (12.68%) up 50% YoY, finance cost down to 4.81% after loan payoff
Revenue guidance for FY27 is around Rs 570 crore (16-17% growth) with a +/-5% range; management expects 15-20% annual growth going forward.
Management does not revise guidance mid-year; expects to perform well within the guided range.
EBITDA margins around 18-19% sustained for a long time; management aspires to maintain them but acknowledges quarterly volatility of ~2 percentage points.
FY27 capex of Rs 77 crore: Rs 35-40 crore for heat treatment replacement, Rs 35 crore for capacity expansion; next year's capex to be announced in January.
Capex is announced annually; FY28 capex will be communicated in January; investments made today support growth in FY28-29.
Capacity expansion from current capex will come online partly in FY27 and partly in FY28.
Project Venus (electric sports car) Level 1 approval granted; final approval expected 24 Oct; pilot suppliers already shipping parts by sea.
KTM volumes recovered to respectable levels; forecast for coming months very good; new Duke 790 launched with good US acceptance.
BMW export orders: RACL is sole supplier for each component until end of life per formal agreement.
